repo_path_false_positive_surface.note: the repo_path guard refuses any component that merely *mentions* a denylisted word, so descriptive evidence names are now refused. The branch review/credential-literals-gate exists in this very repo -- a publish under evidence/credential-literals-gate/ would be refused. The old guard had this property for LOCAL names only.

verdict.core_fix_basis: repo_path now goes through the single `_name_refusal` helper (source-level: 3 call sites, one helper, shown in the old->new diff); dirty repo_path refused in-process and at the CLI with rc=5; CLEAN/CLEAN still allowed; the six pre-existing boundaries still refuse; and zero PUT is confirmed OUT OF BAND from branch state (5 targets 404, parent dir has exactly the 2 published entries).

corrections.what: M1_repo_path_guard_removed and M2_local_only_regression are observationally the SAME mutant: M1 deletes the loop, M2 rewrites its iterable to `([] if False else [])`; in both cases the loop body never runs. Measured: the full 7-input battery is identical for the two mutants, and the receipt itself reports identical `mutation_arms` readings.
corrections.consequence: the two killer rows are ONE piece of evidence reported twice, not two. The claim that they are `各自` (each) independent is not supported.
corrections.also: M2's label names a mutation that was not performed -- nothing in it is 'local only'. Neither arm touches `_name_refusal`'s scope argument.

corrections.what: `cell5_single_helper_both_scopes` = LOCAL_NAME_DIRTY_refused and REPO_PATH_DIRTY_refused, i.e. 'both scopes refuse'. That predicate is equally satisfied by two duplicated denylists.
corrections.consequence: the cell does not measure 'single helper'. The arm that WOULD make it load-bearing is missing; I built it (M3: `_name_refusal` returns None) and it flips BOTH scopes (local_dirty true->false, repo_dirty true->false) while every REGRESSION_* stays refused -- so the implementation is a single helper, but the published receipt contains no evidence of that.
corrections.suggested_arm: M3_shared_helper_mutated, expectation: both scope cells go green, regressions held.

corrections.what: the file docstring states 'call() is stubbed and the PUT invocation count is asserted mechanically'. Neither is true: there is no stub and no count. The predicate actually used is a stdout substring test for the exact literal 'PUT -> 201', and the SAME key is set to literal True in the branch where the CLI is skipped -- so cell6 is satisfied when a case never ran at all.
corrections.measured: feeding the predicate a stdout that really contains a PUT attempt with a non-201 status (`PUT -> 403 commit=`) returns True, i.e. it reads as 'no upload'. For `PUT -> 201` it correctly returns False, so the predicate is not dead -- it is just narrower than its name.
corrections.consequence: the 'zero PUT' claim is TRUE (I proved it out of band) but this cell does not prove it. Keep the claim; re-attribute the evidence, or make the instrument count invocations (e.g. stub `call` and assert its PUT count == 0).

corrections.what: cell3 (CLEAN/CLEAN) is in-process only (`mod.guard(...) is None`). No CLI-level positive control exists, so the CLI's rc=5 cells are equally satisfied by a CLI that refuses everything and never uploads.
corrections.consequence: this is precisely the failure the instrument's own docstring warns about ('the safest publisher is one that uploads nothing'), applied one layer down.
corrections.suggested_arm: one CLEAN/CLEAN CLI run against a throw-away target on a scratch branch, asserting the PUT really happened -- or, cheaper, a stubbed `call` that records the PUT.

registered_side_effect_ruling.asked: paths already published that contain a forbidden fragment (e.g. `evidence/ord0263-s5fix-laneB/s5fix_read_live.json`) can no longer be re-published at the same path. Defect or not?
registered_side_effect_ruling.ruling: NOT a defect of ORD-0275. It is a correctly-registered consequence.
why: the guard is fail-closed and fires before any network call: in the new publisher, guard() returns before the initial GET, so even the 'already identical - nothing to push' early return is unreachable for a forbidden path;

'the path already exists on the branch' is an UNSAFE exemption predicate: this tool is not the only writer to commander/control (the GitHub API and UI are), so path existence is partly controlled by whoever can write -- an existence-based exemption converts into a bypass;
the chosen handling (publish under a new name, leave the old path untouched) is the right one and already matches the fragment notice's own advice.
registered_side_effect_ruling.if_an_exemption_is_wanted: it needs its own order, its own cell and its own counter-control; it must not be keyed on path existence. Scope-limited out of 0275 is correct.

false_positive_surface_measured.note: broader than the one case that was registered: any component that merely MENTIONS a denylisted word is refused. Measured on 17 components drawn from real paths in this project -> 8 refused.
false_positive_surface_measured.notable: `credential-literals-gate` is the name of a branch that exists in this very repo, so a publish under evidence/credential-literals-gate/ would now be refused.
